IAL is recorded as `unknown` rather than IAL1 because the condition is inapplicability, not indeterminacy: no user identity is ever collected, so no proofing process exists to grade. NIST 800-63A IAL1 ('self-asserted, no proofing') still presupposes an asserted identity, which this application never receives. The schema's nist_ial enum (IAL1|IAL2|IAL3|unknown) has no `not-applicable` member, so `unknown` is the only expressible honest value - see references/nist-800-63-mapping.md 'Unknown' section.

AAL is recorded as `below-AAL1` (not `unknown`) because the authenticator configuration WAS determined: there is no authenticator of any kind, which is by definition weaker than the single-factor AAL1 floor of NIST 800-63B.
FAL is `not-applicable` per references/nist-800-63-mapping.md ('Local accounts only (no federation) -> not-applicable'). This application has neither local accounts nor federation.

model_type is deliberately OMITTED rather than guessed. The enum (federated, on-prem-directory, custom-app-specific, mfa-addon, cert-based, social, saas-idp) has no member meaning 'no identity mechanism present'. Selecting `custom-app-specific` would falsely assert that this application implemented its own authentication; it implemented none. The field is optional in schemas/discovery/identity-landscape.schema.json, so it is left out.

user_classes is `local-host-operator`, meaning any OS principal holding execute permission on the built binary. This is not an application-defined user class - the application has none. Corroborated by the catalog entry's `user_facing: false` and `archetype: cli` (input-artifacts/.../discovery/d634afdb-97cc-4589-a080-5766d4f377d5/catalog.json:36,57).

assurance_gaps.description: The application performs NO authentication at all - this is materially stronger than the `no-mfa` label implies. There is no primary factor, no user registration, no session, and no authorization check on any code path; `no-mfa` is simply the closest available member of the gap_type enum, which has no value meaning 'no authentication layer whatsoever', and it therefore UNDERSTATES the condition. Severity is set to `low` on the current architecture, not on the label: the component is a non-user-facing console executable (catalog.json:36,57) with no HTTP listener, no database, no scheduler, no network egress, no persistence, and no PII or PHI in scope; it seeds a hardcoded list of fictional inventory items (Program.cs:14-27) and exits. Access is fully delegated to host-OS execute permission, which is a defensible control for a single-run local CLI. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this severity is PROVISIONAL. The skill's quality rule requires severity to be pinned to the application's risk tier, and no authoritative risk tier was available - the catalog entry records `safety_tier: null` and notes that profiles/faa/risk-classification.yaml explicitly prohibits inferring safety tier from code patterns alone (catalog.json:56,61). If a tier is subsequently assigned, this severity MUST be re-pinned; a Tier 1 designation would make a below-AAL1 model `critical`, not `low`.
assurance_gaps.remediation_recommendation: Take no identity remediation action against the application as it exists today - there is no authenticated subject to strengthen, and adding an identity layer to a self-contained local CLI would add attack surface without reducing risk. Instead treat this as a conditional gate on disposition: IF the application is re-platformed into anything networked or multi-user (a web front end, an API, or a shared service), an identity model must be designed from zero and integrated with the FAA broker pattern before that deployment, targeting AAL2 minimum for a Tier 2 workload and AAL3 (phishing-resistant, PIV on-card) for any Tier 1 workload per references/retire-recommendations.md. Until then, document host-OS execute permission as the operative access control and obtain the missing risk-tier classification so this severity can be pinned rather than estimated.

broker_recommendation.broker_technology: None for the current architecture. If and only if this application is re-platformed as a networked, multi-user service, the FAA profile default applies: Keycloak 24.x on AWS GovCloud (references/faa-identity-providers.md:47-48). No broker is recommended for, or deployable against, the console executable that exists today.
broker_recommendation.rationale:
SCOPE. This is a per-application invocation of identity-landscape-analyzer (skill scope note LD-10), so it sees one application's identity model and cannot and does not decide the FAA portfolio's broker posture. Nothing here should be read as dissent from a portfolio-level decision.

WHY keep-separate. `keep-separate` is recorded because there is nothing to broker. A federated broker works by intercepting an authentication redirect and exchanging an assertion; this application never authenticates anyone. Its only entry point is a console Main() that builds a hardcoded item list and exits (src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:8,33), with no HTTP listener, no IDP integration, and no authentication libraries linked (csproj:35-41). Fronting it with Keycloak is not a deferred improvement - it is architecturally undefined. fronted_idps is therefore an empty array, because zero upstream IDPs are or could be fronted for this application in its present form; it is NOT a placeholder for the profile's default pair.

RELATIONSHIP TO THE FAA PROFILE DEFAULT. The profile default is `broker-all` unless an application opts out with ATO evidence (references/faa-identity-providers.md:45-46). That opt-out clause is expressly NOT being invoked: no ATO evidence was supplied and none is claimed. This is a finding of architectural inapplicability, not an exemption. If this application is modernized into a networked service it should join `broker-all` on the profile's terms - Keycloak 24.x on AWS GovCloud fronting Login.gov (IAL2/AAL2/FAL2) for any public-user class and PIV via MyAccess (IAL3/AAL3/FAL2+, on-card and PIN-unlocked) for any agency-staff class, per references/faa-identity-providers.md:11-25.

MIGRATION COMPLEXITY. `low`, in the specific sense that there is no migration to perform. retire_recommendations is an empty array because no identity model exists to retire: there is no email-code MFA model, no app-native password store, and - checked explicitly, since a retire recommendation for it would have been mandatory rather than optional - no IWA/NTLM, no direct LDAP bind, no Kerberos, and no local users table anywhere in the tree. There are consequently no accounts to link, no directories to merge, and no users to re-badge, which are the drivers of the medium-through-very-high bands in references/retire-recommendations.md. If a future re-platform introduces authentication, complexity should be re-scored then against the real user population; it cannot be scored against a population of zero now.

PROLIFERATION. proliferation_findings is an empty array, and this is a deliberate scoping decision rather than an unexamined one. All six heuristics in references/proliferation-patterns.md were evaluated and none fires on this application's own evidence: same-user-multiple-accounts requires accounts (there are none); same-app-multiple-models requires 2+ models for one user class (there is one model, and it is the absence of authentication); redundant-federation requires two federation IDPs (there are zero); legacy-directory-without-sso requires a direct ldap:// bind, NTLM/Kerberos IWA, or a local users table (grep found none); no-broker-federation requires 3+ distinct providers in the observed set (there are zero). identity-model-per-app is a ratio-of-models-to-apps measure that is only computable at portfolio scope, and per LD-10 a portfolio-wide count must not be asserted from a single application's evidence - so although the FAA reference records that the Phase 1 portfolio scored above the 0.6 threshold (references/faa-identity-providers.md:37-40), that is profile background, not something this invocation measured, and it is not emitted here as a finding whose affected_apps would list applications outside this scope.

DATA-QUALITY CAVEATS a reviewer must resolve. (1) portfolio_id is recorded as UNKNOWN because no portfolio identifier was supplied in the dispatch context; rather than invent one that would silently fail to bind downstream, the field carries an explicit self-describing UNKNOWN string. (2) The FAA identity-provider reference declares `applies-to: [iacra, cais, aadocs, medxpress, dms, rms, ims]` (references/faa-identity-providers.md:5) and this application is not among them, so the profile's canonical IDP bindings are cited above only as the forward-looking target state, never as observed configuration. (3) profiles/faa/ was not materialized in this workspace, so no citation is made to profiles/faa/compliance.yaml or profiles/faa/config/identity-landscape-analyzer.yaml even though the reference's citation-format section prefers that form; only files actually read are cited. (4) The source tree is the public 'Gilded Rose Refactoring Kata' with no aviation or FAA nexus, which the catalog entry independently flags (catalog.json:59-60); whether this application_id maps to a genuine FAA system is unconfirmed and should be settled before this artifact is consumed.
